thread:
liz_support: FYI customer_acme hitting sustained throughput drops on Dedicated this morning, started ~07:10 their TZ. Reports: increased latency, intermittent 429s, and a lot of tiny microbatches in the logs. They say their QPS is steady but tokens/sec fell ~40%.

mike_oncall: Can you paste the top errors and any request IDs?

liz_support: Here are snippets from their support dump: 
```
error: Request throttled (capacity_exceeded)
request_id: r-0a1b2c3d
avg_latency_tokens_ms: 120
observed_batch_sizes: [1,1,2,1,1,1]
continuous_batcher_state: prefill=0.2, drain=0.05
max_batch_tokens: 4096
```
They also included a trace link: https://console.internal/redwood/trace/r-0a1b2c3d

ryan_sre: Thanks. Those microbatches + low prefill fraction smell like the scheduler is favoring latency over packing and the max_batch_tokens ceiling isn't being reached due to per-request token limits. Could be scheduler tuning regression or noisy neighbor starving GPU cycles.

sara_eng: Quick checks: 1) were autoscaler events around the timeframe? 2) any change to batcher config pushed in the last deploy?

liz_support: Customer said they didn't change client side. Deploy-bot shows no canary for runtime in the last 6 hours.

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] No new runtime canaries in the window 2025-10-03T06:00-12:00Z.

mike_oncall: OK runbook: get queue metrics + per-worker CPU/GPU utilization, continuous-batcher histograms, and the scheduler weights. Can you run the quick query and paste results? (I can run if you want).

liz_support: Pasting output from internal metrics query (abridged): 
```
/metrics?cluster=dedicated-acme&window=30m
continuous_batcher.microbatch_count: 8450
continuous_batcher.avg_microbatch_size: 1.8
scheduler.prefill_fraction: 0.18
scheduler.max_wait_ms: 6
worker.gpu_util_pct: [45,42,47,12,13]
autoscaler.scale_events: []
```
Note two workers are low GPU util (12,13) while others are ~45.

ryan_sre: That matches noisy-tenant symptoms. A few workers pinned at low GPU util suggests contention or preemption on those nodes. Check cgroup/oom events and host-level processes. Also look at process-level CPU steal.

sara_eng: Also, scheduler.max_wait_ms=6 is pretty strict. With many short requests that penalizes packing. If requests are bursty with small token counts, we'll get lots of tiny microbatches. Proposed mitigation: temporarily relax max_wait_ms to 20-30 ms and increase prefill_fraction to 0.35 so continuous-batcher waits a bit to fill. That should increase throughput while adding small latency tail.

mike_oncall: +1. Steps to repro locally: 1) run load generator with 300rps of 8-30 token requests, 2) set scheduler.max_wait_ms=6 and observe avg microbatch size, 3) change to 25 and compare. Use the perf tool:
```
perfctl --target dedicated-acme --load qps=300 --tokens=rand(8,30) --duration=5m
perfctl get continuous-batcher-stats --target dedicated-acme
```
If you can repro, we can hotfix config.

liz_support: Customer agreed to a short trial. Running perfctl now. Will report in ~6m. :hourglass_flowing_sand: 

(6m later)

liz_support: Repro done. With max_wait_ms=6 avg_microbatch_size=1.7, with max_wait_ms=25 avg_microbatch_size=5.2 and tokens/sec +36%, 429s dropped to near zero.

ryan_sre: Nice. That strongly indicates scheduler timing floor was the cause. But we still have 2 low-GPU nodes; create a ticket to investigate host-level noisy processes. Maybe autoscaler didn't rebalance because we pin pods by affinity.

sara_eng: For short-term customer mitigation we should: 1) push a config change to dedicated-acme runtime (scheduler.max_wait_ms=25, prefill_fraction=0.35), 2) monitor latencies (p95) for 30m, 3) if stable, apply to their dedicated pool as standard. I'll prepare the rollout.

mike_oncall: Make sure to set a canary in the pool: 5% traffic shift for 10m then auto-promote. Use the console rollout: 
```
POST /api/rollout
{ "target":"dedicated-acme", "changes": {"scheduler.max_wait_ms":25, "scheduler.prefill_fraction":0.35 }, "canary_pct":5, "canary_window_mins":10 }
```
Add a fallback to previous config if 5xx rate > 0.5% or p95 increases > 30%.

liz_support: Actioned. Customer confirmed noticeable improvement.

ryan_sre: Filed infra ticket INF-5123 to dig into the two low-GPU hosts (possible noisy neighbor or host-level daemon running backups). Add the host-level metrics and strace logs if needed.

sara_eng: We'll follow up on the host ticket, but closing this customer-facing escalation after config canary completes. Leave notes for Dedicated runbook about defaulting scheduler.max_wait_ms policy for token-light workloads.

mike_oncall: Thanks everyone. Final note: consider adding a detection alert that triggers when avg_microbatch_size < 2.5 for > 5m while overall qps stable — auto-suggest scheduler tuning to SEs. :robot_face:

customer_acme: Thanks for the quick help—saw throughput back to normal after the change. Appreciate the fast turnaround! :tada:
